title: Honda (1971) J. Theor. Biol., Honda & Fisher (1978) Science, Fisher & Honda (1979) Am. J. Bot., Shinozaki et al. (1964) & Eloy (2011) Phys. Rev. Lett. — 3D Recursive Dichotomous Tree Morphogenesis, Effective Leaf Area Optimization & Leonardo da Vinci Pipe-Model Area Conservation
organism: Cornus controversa (Pagoda dogwood / wedding cake tree) & Terminalia catappa (Tropical almond pagoda tree)

primary_sources.role: 3D vector-rotation recursive model of dichotomous botanical tree architecture parameterized by daughter divergence angles (theta_1, theta_2), length contraction ratios (r_1, r_2), and vertical phyllotactic divergence angle alpha = 137.5 deg in the local horizontal plane spanned by v and v x z_hat

Demonstrates that empirical branching angles (theta_1 approx 24-32 deg, theta_2 approx 52-62 deg) and contraction ratios (r_1 = 0.90, r_2 = 0.70) in tiered pagoda crowns (Terminalia catappa, Cornus controversa) maximize projected non-overlapping effective leaf area A_eff / A_total across 5-branch horizontal whorls

primary_sources.citation: Fisher & Honda (1979) American Journal of Botany 66(6):633-644
primary_sources.role: Systematic 2D parameter-space survey of (theta_1, theta_2) and (r_1, r_2) across sympodial Terminalia-type horizontal branching tiers quantifying intra-branch and inter-whorl leaf cluster self-shading

primary_sources.citation: Shinozaki, Yoda, Hozumi & Kira (1964) Japanese Journal of Ecology 14(3):97-105
primary_sources.role: Pipe-model theory of plant form establishing cross-sectional sapwood area conservation d_parent^2 = d_1^2 + d_2^2 linking unit vascular pipes to supported terminal leaf clusters

Biomechanical derivation of Leonardo da Vinci's cross-sectional area-preserving rule (sum d_i^Delta = d_0^Delta with Delta approx 1.8-2.0) under uniform wind-induced bending stress in self-similar fractal tree crowns

honda_fisher_1978_angle_sweep_benchmarks.description: Degenerate collinear zero-angle ablation (theta_1 = theta_2 = 0 deg): all 16 leaf clusters per primary branch superpose along a single radial line
Sub-optimal narrow divergence angle regime with severe intra-sector leaf cluster self-shading
Intermediate divergence angle regime approaching sector filling
Empirical Cornus controversa horizontal pagoda tier branching angles maximizing non-overlapping canopy display
Honda & Fisher (1978) Science global maximum of effective leaf area A_eff / A_total in Terminalia catappa
Wide divergence regime where outer secondary twigs begin crossing adjacent 72 deg whorl sector boundaries
Over-wide divergence regime exhibiting inter-branch collision across neighboring whorl sectors
Extreme wide divergence causing retrograde twig back-folding and heavy secondary self-shading

honda_1971_3d_archetype_benchmarks.label: Excurrent Conifer (Abies / Picea)
honda_1971_3d_archetype_benchmarks.description: Strong apical dominance (theta_1 = 8 deg, r_1 = 0.88) with steep conical lateral branches

honda_1971_3d_archetype_benchmarks.label: Pagoda Tiered Crown (Cornus controversa / Terminalia)
honda_1971_3d_archetype_benchmarks.description: Stratified horizontal pagoda tiers maximizing planar effective leaf area A_eff / A_total

honda_1971_3d_archetype_benchmarks.label: Decurrent Deliquescent Hardwood (Quercus / Ulmus)
honda_1971_3d_archetype_benchmarks.description: Sub-equal dichotomous forks (theta_1 approx theta_2, r_1 approx r_2) forming a rounded dome-shaped canopy

honda_1971_3d_archetype_benchmarks.label: Weeping Pendulous Crown (Salix babylonica)
honda_1971_3d_archetype_benchmarks.description: High secondary divergence angle coupled with distally accumulating gravitropic/elastic droop
